statement: Love Me Forever is the debut studio album by the American rock band Pinkshift, released on October 21, 2022.
Pinkshift began writing their debut album in late 2020.
Pinkshift signed to Hopeless Records in 2021.
Love Me Forever was recorded in March 2022 with producer Will Yip at Studio 4 in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania.
Love Me Forever sees Pinkshift expand their musical range beyond the pop-punk style of their early releases into alternative rock, emo, grunge, hard rock, indie rock, and post-hardcore.
Its lyrics explore social topics including abusive relationships, trauma, alienation, social media, and coming of age in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Music critics praised Pinkshift's catchy songwriting and energetic performances on Love Me Forever.
Alternative Press and Kerrang! listed the album as one of the best of 2022.
BrooklynVegan and Paste ranked it as one of the year's best punk albums.
The album was supported by four singles, "Nothing (In My Head)", "I'm Not Crying You're Crying", "Get Out", and "In a Breath".
Pinkshift embarked on a headlining tour of North America in support of the album, The Forever Tour, between October and November 2022.
An extended play (EP) of remixes, Love Me for the Summer, was released in July 2024.
Vocalist Ashrita Kumar met guitarist Paul Vallejo and began writing songs under the alias Sugar Crisis in 2018.
The following year, they found drummer Myron Houngbedji and formed Pinkshift.
All three members were attending the Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland.
After recruiting bassist Erich Weinroth, Pinkshift began playing live shows in late 2019.
In August 2020, the band's single "I'm Gonna Tell My Therapist on You" achieved viral success.
The viral success of "I'm Gonna Tell My Therapist on You" helped Pinkshift become one of the biggest breakout names on the pop-punk scene, according to Mia Hughes of NME.
The song also brought the band to the attention of Eric Tobin, the head of A&R at Hopeless Records.
In 2021, Pinkshift self-released their debut extended play Saccharine.
Pinkshift went on tour supporting Mannequin Pussy in 2021.
During the tour supporting Mannequin Pussy, Pinkshift met with Tobin and other members of Hopeless.
Pinkshift decided to sign with Hopeless Records during their tour supporting Mannequin Pussy.
Weinroth departed the band soon after the EP's release.
Pinkshift began writing Love Me Forever in late 2020.
Pinkshift recorded three demos with producer Will Yip in March 2021.
The band performed several songs from the album during their shows in 2021.
With the exception of "In a Breath", the album's songs were written by Kumar, Vallejo, and Houngbedji.
Kumar, Vallejo, and Houngbedji worked collaboratively on the album's songs.
Kumar handled lyrics for the album's songs.
Houngbedji handled drums for the album's songs.
Whilst working on the album, Houngbedji drew influence from hardcore music, Kublai Khan, Turnstile, Knocked Loose, and Roland TR-808 drum patterns in hip-hop music.
Vallejo cited Microwave, Pierce the Veil, and Citizen as influences on his guitar playing during this time.
Kumar began playing guitar shortly after the release of Saccharine.
Kumar playing guitar resulted in an increased grunge influence in Pinkshift's songwriting from bands such as Nirvana and Soundgarden.
Pinkshift was heavily inspired by the Arctic Monkeys, specifically their albums Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not (2006) and Favourite Worst Nightmare (2007).
Pinkshift's experiences of coming of age in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic served as additional influences on the lyrics.
What Pinkshift saw as "injustices and failings" by the United States government during the COVID-19 pandemic served as additional influences on the lyrics.
Pinkshift recorded Love Me Forever with Yip over the course of three weeks in March 2022.
Love Me Forever was recorded at Studio 4 in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania.
The recording of Love Me Forever marked the first time the band worked in a proper recording studio.
Houngbedji recorded his drum tracks within a week.
After Houngbedji recorded his drum tracks, the bass and guitars were tracked.
Kumar likened recording to a summer camp.
Kumar likened Yip to a coach.
Pinkshift had completed 90% of the album's material before going into the studio.
Yip encouraged Pinkshift to push themselves performance and songwriting-wise.
Kumar said that Yip shared similar influences with Pinkshift.
Kumar said that Yip helped "exemplify the core" of their songs.
Houngbedji said he connected well with Yip as they were both drummers.
Houngbedji credited Yip with making his playing style more precise and specific.
Recording was completed days before Pinkshift embarked on a two-month-long tour supporting PUP.
Pinkshift's two-month-long tour supporting PUP began on April 1, 2022.
Love Me Forever has been described as alternative rock, emo, grunge, hard rock, indie rock, pop-punk, and post-hardcore.
Pinkshift intended to display their musical range beyond the pop-punk style of their early releases.
Pinkshift intended to potentially expand the pop-punk genre's limitations.
Pinkshift did not reject their association with pop-punk.
The album's songs are generally fast-paced.
The album's songs are marked by "jagged" guitars.
The album's songs are marked by melodic elements.
The album's songs are marked by guitar solos.
The album's songs are marked by hard-hitting drums.
The album's songs are marked by "expressive" vocals.
The album's lyrics predominately express feelings of anger, angst, and anguish.
The album's lyrics balance "vulnerability and defiance", according to Vicky Greer of New Noise Magazine.
Kumar said that the lyrics primarily dealt with the experience of being alive.

Kumar stated in an interview with Goucher College's Revelance blog that "Even though you do have rage at these big systems of oppression, it becomes a personal rage because you're personally targeted if you're anything other than a cis white guy".
Kumar said the album's title was meant to highlight the fact that "no one is going to love you more than you love yourself".
Love Me Forever opens with "I'm Not Crying You're Crying".
"I'm Not Crying You're Crying" is a heavy, energetic song.
"I'm Not Crying You're Crying" is about struggling and being distrustful of those offering help.
Kumar said "I'm Not Crying You're Crying" was the only song on the album to come exclusively from a place of "raw and unfiltered emotion".
"Nothing (In My Head)" is about wanting to escape from a place of feeling trapped.
"Nothing (In My Head)" is about social media addiction.
David Renshaw of The Fader called "Nothing (In My Head)" an "heavy AF ode to turning off your devices and embracing the smooth brain lifestyle".
The song's guitars and vocals were heavily inspired by the Nirvana song "Breed".
Kumar had to rewrite the song's original melody and lyrics due to them being too similar to "Breed".
Kumar described "Get Out" as a call to reclaim one's means of autonomy and self-expression from white supremacist and patriarchal hierarchies.
Nick Ruskell of Kerrang! described "Cherry (We're All Gonna Die)" as reminiscent of Turnstile "with bigger choruses".
"The Kids Aren't Alright" is titled after the song of the same name by The Offspring.
"The Kids Aren't Alright" is a "war cry".
"The Kids Aren't Alright" is marked by aggressive musicianship and vocals.
Kumar said "The Kids Aren't Alright" marks the point at which the lyrics on Love Me Forever move from vague feelings into specificity and identify what is wrong.
"Trust Fall" details an abusive relationship.
"Trust Fall" is about "realizing [...] the anger that you feel after going through something that wasn't fair".
"In a Breath" is an introspective piano ballad.
"In a Breath" is centered around Kumar's experiences dealing with trauma, bodily dissasociation, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the aftermath of an abusive relationship.
Kumar wrote "In a Breath" in 2018.
Kumar continued to revisit "In a Breath" for comfort until deciding to present it to the other members of Pinkshift.
Houngbedji said the band included "In a Breath" on Love Me Forever as they felt it fit the album's thematic context.
Houngbedji said "In a Breath" sounds unlike the rest of the album's songs.
"Cinderella" is a slow-paced song.
"Cinderella" sees Kumar wishing they could erase memories of someone who betrayed them.
Greer compared "Cinderella"'s dynamics to Evanescence and New Years Day.
"Burn the Witch" is a narrative-driven song.
"Burn the Witch" was inspired by Kumar's experience of having their friends turn against them.
Kumar's friends turned against them after a member of their dance team began spreading false rumors about them whilst they were ill.
Abby Jones of Consequence viewed "Burn the Witch"'s lyrics as analyzing groupthink's "disproportionate maliciousness" towards women.
The album's title track is rooted in pop-punk.
"Let Me Drown" displays hardcore influences.
The demo of "Let Me Drown" was heavily inspired by the Heart Attack Man song "Puke".
Aliya Chaudry of Stereogum viewed the album's final track, "Dreamer", as "signifying the journey of coming to terms with challenges and making it through to the other side".
Pinkshift wrote "Dreamer" through jamming.
Pinkshift sought to make "something that people could dance to" with "Dreamer", according to Kumar.
The lyrics of "Dreamer" were influenced by the Arctic Monkeys song "A Certain Romance".
On June 1, 2022, Pinkshift announced their signing to Hopeless Records.
On June 1, 2022, Pinkshift released the lead single from Love Me Forever, "Nothing (In My Head)".
On July 13, Pinkshift announced the album Love Me Forever.
On July 13, Pinkshift released "I'm Not Crying You're Crying".
Love Me Forever was released on October 21, 2022, following the release of two further singles, "Get Out" and "In a Breath".
On July 11, 2024, Pinkshift released Love Me for the Summer.
Love Me for the Summer is an EP featuring remixes by Caco of five of the album's songs.
The remixes on Love Me for the Summer are in a variety of styles including trap, house, and dariacore.
Preceding the release of Love Me Forever, Pinkshift played four shows opening for Destroy Boys on the east coast of the United States.
Pinkshift performed at the Emo Nite New Orleans Vacation in September 2022.
Pinkshift performed alongside Bring Me the Horizon and 100 gecs at the Emo Nite New Orleans Vacation.
From October 20 and November 19, 2022, the band embarked on their debut headlining tour of the United States, the Forever Tour.
The Forever Tour saw Kumar performing guitar onstage for the first time.
The band were supported by Jigsaw Youth and Yasmin Nur on the Forever Tour.
Yasmin Nur dropped off the Forever Tour early on.
Greer of New Noise Magazine called Love Me Forever "a beautifully complex record that shows off the seemingly limitless talent" of Pinkshift's members.
Ruskell of Kerrang! said the album's "sharp, skilful [sic] and bristling with infectious energy".
Ruskell considered Love Me Forever a promising debut album.
Emma Wilkes of Stereoboard wrote that Love Me Forever was one of the best rock debuts of 2022.
Emma Wilkes placed particular praise on Kumar's vocals and the record's "genuine trendless individuality".
Mia Hughes of NME remarked that Pinkshift's "sonics are [shown to be] wider-ranging and more exciting than ever" on the album.
Alessandro DeCaro of Alternative Press felt Love Me Forever's stylistic range and the band's "unique arrangement skills" broadened its appeal.
Under the Radar reviewer Caleb Campbell highlighted the performances of its members and the album's balance between "searing energy and visceral vulnerability".
Jones of Consequence praised the album's production and themes.
Jones called Love Me Forever a "useful companion for the world's downfall".
BrooklynVegan's Andrew Sacher remarked that Pinkshift had "a knack for writing pop music that you can rock the fuck out to".
Andrew Sacher remarked that Pinkshift sounded both heavier and catchier on Love Me Forever compared to Saccharine, courtesy of Yip's production.
Jenny Josefine Schulz of Ox-Fanzine thought the album's vocals lacked depth.
Jenny Josefine Schulz thought the album made up for the lack of vocal depth with "truly atmospheric, catchy instrumentals".
Love Me Forever was listed as one of the best albums of 2022 by Alternative Press and Kerrang!
BrooklynVegan and Paste ranked Love Me Forever as one of the years' best punk albums.
Loudwire listed Love Me Forever as one of the year's best rock and metal debut albums.
The members of Magnolia Park listed Love Me Forever as one of their favourite albums of the year.
"Nothing (In My Head)" was included in Vulture's list of the best songs of 2022.
